title: Nested Loops: Loops Inside Loops
learningObjectives: Explain how an inner loop runs each time the outer loop advances.
Trace nested loops to count total inner-body executions.
Use nested loops to create row-and-column patterns.
Predict output order by tracking both loop counters.
Recognize when nesting adds unnecessary work or makes logic difficult to follow.

understand.concept: A nested loop is a loop placed inside the body of another loop. The outer loop controls larger steps, such as rows, while the inner loop completes its own repetitions for each outer iteration. When the inner loop finishes, the outer loop updates and begins the next iteration; the inner loop starts again from its initialization.
understand.whyItMatters: Nested loops are useful for repeated combinations, grids, tables, patterns, and comparing items in two collections. Understanding which loop controls which repetition helps predict output and avoid mistakes.
understand.analogy: Imagine arranging seats in a hall: for each row, you visit every seat from left to right; only after the row is complete do you move to the next row.
understand.analogyLimit: The inner loop is not always a fixed number of steps. It may depend on the outer counter, and nested loops can contain more than two levels although deep nesting can be hard to read.

explain.narrative: In a nested loop, the outer body begins an iteration and then reaches the inner loop. The inner loop runs from its initialization through its condition and update until it ends. Then execution continues in the outer body after the inner loop. The outer loop updates and checks again; if another iteration is allowed, the inner loop runs anew. For two simple loops with independent counts, total inner-body executions equal the outer iteration count multiplied by the inner iteration count.

commonMistakes: Assuming the inner loop runs only once in total instead of once per outer iteration.
Resetting or updating an outer counter inside the inner body by accident.
Using the wrong counter in a condition or output expression.
Forgetting that the inner loop starts again for each outer iteration.
Adding unnecessary nesting that makes code harder to read or more expensive.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Make a 3-row number grid
guidedTask.instructions: Use nested loops to print a 3-row grid. Each row should contain the numbers 1, 2, and 3 separated by spaces.
steps: Create an outer loop that runs for three rows.
Create an inner loop that runs for three columns.
Build a row string inside the outer loop.
Add each column number and a space to the row string.
Print the completed row after the inner loop finishes.

independentTask.title: Independent: Multiplication table segment
independentTask.instructions: Write nested loops that print a 4-by-4 multiplication table for numbers 1 through 4. Each row should show four products.
requirements: Use an outer loop for the row multiplier 1 through 4.
Use an inner loop for the column multiplier 1 through 4.
Calculate each product using both counters.
Keep a row string so each table row appears on one line.
Print each completed row after the inner loop ends.

hints: The outer loop starts one row at a time.
The inner loop finishes all of its work before the outer loop moves on.
Reset the row string at the start of every outer iteration.
Use both counters in the inner calculation.
For independent loops, total inner-body runs are outer count multiplied by inner count.
Trace a small grid with two rows and two columns before attempting a larger one.

questions.prompt: When does the inner loop normally run in a two-level nested loop?
options: Only once before the outer loop starts
To completion for each outer-loop iteration
Only after the outer loop finishes
questions.answer: To completion for each outer-loop iteration
questions.explanation: Each time the outer body reaches the inner loop, the inner loop runs until its own condition becomes false.

questions.prompt: If the outer loop runs 4 times and the inner loop runs 3 times per outer iteration, how many inner-body executions occur?
What is the output order for a standard row-and-column nested loop?
options: All rows finish first, then all columns
Inner values repeat for each outer value
Outer and inner counters change together every time
questions.answer: Inner values repeat for each outer value
questions.explanation: The inner loop completes for one outer value before the outer loop advances.

questions.prompt: Why should a row string usually be reset inside the outer loop when printing a pattern?
options: So each row starts empty before its columns are added
So the outer loop stops earlier
To make the inner loop skip its first iteration
questions.answer: So each row starts empty before its columns are added
questions.explanation: Resetting inside the outer loop prevents previous-row text from carrying into the next row.

questions.prompt: What can happen when loops are nested unnecessarily deeply?
options: Code may become harder to understand and require more work
The inner loop automatically becomes a function
questions.answer: Code may become harder to understand and require more work
questions.explanation: Nesting increases repeated work and complexity, so use only the levels needed.
